API and SDK
Code node
The code node allows you to generate return values by writing your own code. Coze enhances this functionality by enabling the use of IDE tools within the code node, where the AI capability can automatically generate code or you can write custom code logic to process input parameters and return results.​
Configure the code node​
Here are the parameters for configuring a code node:​
​
Setting​
	
Description​


Input​
	
Declare the variables needed in your code. When adding input parameters, specify the parameter name and variable value. The variable value can be a fixed value or reference the output parameters of previous nodes.​
Note
In your code, you can access these input parameters directly using params['input']​
​


Code​
	
Write the code snippets to be executed within the code node. You can either write the code manually or use AI to generate code. ​
Reference variables: Reference input parameters as variables directly within the code to process and return the result as an object.​
Function restriction: Only single-function code is supported. Even if only one output value is returned, the output must be returned as an object.​
Both JavaScript and Python are supported. For more information, see ​Programming Language.​


Output​
	
Define the parameters that will be output once the code runs successfully. You can retain only the required parameters in the output structure according to actual needs.​
Note
Ensure that the parameter names and types you define here match exactly with the return object in the code. Using the default code provided by the code node as an example, the output parameters must align with the return object defined in your code.​
​


​
Caution
Node execution timeout: 60 seconds per request.​
​
Supported programming languages​
The code node supports JavaScript and Python languages.​
JavaScript​
Supports V8 engine Version 11.3.244.8 (Node.js version 20.3.1) and ECMAScript 2022 syntax.​
The code IDE supports TypeScript for a static language coding experience.​
Built-in third-party libraries:​
dayjs (version 1.8.36)​
lodash (version 4.17.20).​
The JavaScript runtime follows the WinterCG specification, supporting various Web APIs including atob(), btoa(), console, setTimeout(), clearTimeout(), structuredClone(), URL, URLSearchParams, AbortController, AbortSignal, TextEncoder, TextDecoder, WebStreams, and WebCrypto (AES, HMAC, SHA algorithms).​
Example code for JavaScript third-party library:​
​
// Only dayjs and lodash are allowed​
import dayjs from 'dayjs';​
import _ from 'lodash';​
 ​
async function main({ params }: Args): Promise<Output> {​
    // Get input params by this way​
    return {​
      content: params.name​
    };​
}​
​
Python​
Based on the Python 3.11.3 standard library, most modules can run normally. The following modules are not supported:​
curses, dbm, ensurepip, fcntl, grp, idlelib, lib2to3, msvcrt, pwd, resource, syslog, termios, tkinter, turtle.py, turtledemo, venv, winreg, winsound, multiprocessing, threading, sockets, pty, and tty.​
Supports built-in third-party libraries:  requests_async and numpy. requests_async is similar to requests(use requests_async with await).​
Note
Python runtime does not currently support HTTP.client requests.​
Using third-party dependencies other than requests_async and numpy is not supported.​
The time.sleep() method is a blocking call and impacts code execution performance. Therefore, we recommend using the asynchronous version asyncio.sleep() instead.​
​
Example in Python:​
​
import requests_async as requests​
​
async def main(args: Args) -> Output:​
    # you can get url by this way​
    url = args.params['url']​
    response = await requests.get(url)​
    ret = {​
      'code': response.status_code,​
      'res': response.text,​
    }​
    return ret​
​
Write code using the code IDE​
Coze provides an online code IDE without the need for code deployment and allows you to focus on code logic. The IDE also offers an AI plugin for code generation.​
To edit and debug code, click the Code setting within the node, and select Edit in IDE.​
​
​
​
​
​
Basic features of the code IDE:​
​
Operation​
	
Description​


Generate code using AI​
	
Click Try AI at the bottom of the IDE and describe your code logic in natural language. The AI will generate the code for you. You can also select a code snippet and use the shortcut key (Command + I for macOS, Ctrl + I for Windows) to let the AI assist in modifying your code.​


Complete the code​
	
With configured input parameters, the IDE supports parameter auto-completion during editing.​


​
Exception handling​
By default, when a node runs into timeout or an exception, the workflow will be interrupted, and error information will be returned in the workflow debugging interface or API. You can also manually configure how to handle scenarios like node timeout, such as timeout duration, whether to retry, or whether to switch to the exception branch.​
​
Exception settings​
	
Description​


Timeout duration​
	
Timeout duration refers to the maximum time a node can run; if it exceeds this duration, the node is considered to have timed out.​
By default, the timeout duration for a node is 60s, i.e., 1 minute. You can also adjust it to 0.1s~60s for more flexible control of the timeout duration.​


Number of retry attempts​
	
When the node runs overtime or encounters an exception, it does not retry by default; you can also set it to retry once.​


Exception Handling Method​
	
When the node runs overtime or encounters an exception, the workflow is interrupted by default. You can also manually modify the exception handling method for this node:​
Interrupt process: The workflow execution is interrupted , and subsequent nodes will no longer run .​
Return preset content: After an exception occurs, the workflow operation will not be interrupted. Developers can customize the necessary output field content to be returned; it must be a field already defined in the output and formatted as legal JSON. Additionally, the node will also return output parameters isSuccess and errorBody, providing detailed information about the node exception.​
Execute exception workflow: After an exception occurs, the workflow operation will not be interrupted but will execute exception workflow analysis instead. Developers need to configure the handling workflow for the newly added exception branch. Exception information will be returned through the node's output parameters isSuccess and errorBody.​


​
​
​
Test run the code node​
When test running the code node, input the parameters and click Run. The platform will execute the code snippet and display the results, including input parameters and the output content
